Ischemic Heart Disease

Slide 25

Indications of surgery:

1. Left main disease more than 50%.

2. Left main equivalent (proximal LAD & proximal Cx more than 70%).

3. 3-vessel disease with left ventricular dysfunction/Diabetes.

4. Failure of medical therapy or percutaneous intervention.

5. Mechanical complications of myocardial infarction.

6. STEMI with cardiogenic shock or on-going ischemia & PCI is not feasible.

7. Associated valve disease.

  • Contraindication to CABG among the options → congestive heart failure with no angina (fixed — the recall keyed cardiogenic shock, but the slide lists STEMI with cardiogenic shock as an INDICATION for CABG when PCI isn't feasible). 427

Added explanationThe left internal mammary artery (LIMA) to the LAD is the gold-standard graft — > 90% patent at 10 years, improves survival. Saphenous vein grafts: ~50–60% patent at 10 years. The radial artery is a second arterial option.
  • Best conduit statement → left internal mammary artery is best for the LAD. 437

Slide 32Valvular Heart Diseases
  • 1. Mitral stenosis:
  • Etiology: Rheumatic, Congenital, L.A. Myxoma
  • The natural progression of MS causes the mitral valve area to reduce by 0.1-0.3 cm per year.
  • The progression from the onset of rheumatic fever to onset of signs of MS takes 10-20 years.
  • The progression from signs of MS to mild symptoms of MS takes 10-20 years.
  • The progression from mild symptoms to de-compensation takes 10-20 years
  • In patients with severe PH the mean survival is 3 years.

Mitral Stenosis

Slide 36
  • Treatment:
  • 1. Medical
  • 2. Balloon mitral valvuloplasty (method of choice when the stenosis is mainly due to fusion of the valve cusps.
  • 3. Open mitral commissurotomy (if PBMV is not feasible or there is associated L.A. thrombus).
  • 4. Mitral valve replacement ( if the leaflets are calcified and fibrotic).
  • 5. Closed mitral commissurotomy (supplanted by PBMV)
  • 6. Trans-catheter (valve-in-valve)procedures to treat bio-prosthetic MS or regurgitation is still in its infancy.

Surgery for Cardio-thoracic Diseases

Slide 37Mitral Stenosis
  • Indications for surgery:
  • Mitral valve surgery for mitral stenosis is recommended for symptomatic severe M.S. when the valve is not favorable for Percutaneous balloon commissurotomy (presence of L.A. clot, significant mitral regurge).

Surgery for Cardio-thoracic Diseases

  • Severe MS (MVA 0.9 cm²), calcified valve + LA clot, stroke → mitral valve replacement (no balloon with a clot or calcification). 437

2. Mitral Regurgitation:

MR is defined as retrograde flow of blood from the LV into the LA due to impaired systolic coaptation between the anterior and posterior leaflets.

Etiology:

1.Rheumatic, Degenerative, Endocarditis

2.Dilatation of the L.V. and mitral valve ring.

3. Dysfunction of the papillary muscle.

4. Congenital abnormalities

5. Calcification of the mitral valve annulus.

Surgery for Cardio-thoracic Diseases

Mitral Regurgitation

Slide 40
  • Asymptomatic patients: can have a long latent period before the onset of symptoms as chronic M.R is well tolerated if L.V. function is still preserved.
  • Symptoms of mitral regurgitation:
  • 1. fatigue and weakness.
  • 2. Dyspnea, Orthopnea, PND
  • 3. Pulmonary hypertension (low C.O.P)
  • 4. Congestive heart failure (L.L. edema, congested neck veins, enlarged tender liver).

Surgery for Cardio-thoracic Diseases

Slide 41Mitral Regurgitation

Signs of mitral regurgitation:

1. displaced apex beat

2. apical thrill

3. apical pan-systolic murmur

4.signs of pulmonary hypertension

Surgery for Cardio-thoracic Diseases

Slide 42Mitral Regurgitation

Indications for surgery:

1.Prompt mitral valve surgery is indicated for the symptomatic patient with acute severe primary MR.

2.In chronic mitral regurge, surgery is done for symptomatic or asymptomatic patients with evidence of LV dysfunction ( E.F <60%, L.V.E.S.D. >40mm, new onset A.F., or pulmonary hypertension.

3.Asymptomatic patients with chronic severe MR and preserved LV (EF>60% and ESD <40mm) in experienced centers with likelihood of repair >95%.

  • Management of acute aortic regurge is by early surgery.
  • Current recommendations for management of chronic AI depend on the presence of symptoms, LV function, and LV dimensions:
  • Symptomatic patients with severe A.R. regardless of left ventricular function
  • Asymptomatic patients with chronic severe A.R. and resting E.F. <55%.
  • A.V.R. is reasonable for asymptomatic patients with severe A.R. with normal LV systolic function but with severe LV dilatation (LVESD> 50 mm).

Infective Endocarditis

Slide 58
  • Infective endocarditis is an infection of cardiovascular structure including valves and intra-cardiac foreign bodies as pacemaker leads, prosthetic valves and surgical patches.
  • It most commonly occurs at sites of previous endocardial damage caused by high pressure jets of blood .
  • Endocarditis of the tricuspid valve occurs in I.V. drug abusers.

Surgery for Cardio-thoracic Diseases

  • Most affected site of bacterial endocarditis → mitral valve (tricuspid in IV drug users). 427

Endocarditis

Slide 59
  • Modified Duke criteria
  • Major criteria:
  • Microbiologic evidence
  • a. Typical microorganisms consistent with IE from 2 separate blood cultures.
  • b. persistently positive blood cultures with other organisms:
  • At least 2 +ve cultures drawn >12 hours apart
  • All 3 or majority of 4 separate cultures with the first and last at least 1 hour apart.
  • Single +ve culture for Coxiella burnetti

Heart Lung Machine

Slide 82
  • Aim of cardiopulmonary bypass:
  • The principal aim of CPB is to facilitate cardiac and thoracic aortic procedures by excluding the heart and lungs from the circulation whilst providing:
  • 1. adequate gas exchange
  • 2. systemic organ perfusion
  • 3. controlling body temp.

Surgery for Cardio-thoracic Diseases

Slide 83Heart Lung Machine
  • Components :
    • Roller pumps
    • Blood Reservoir (cardiotomy reservoir)
    • Oxygenator
    • Heater-cooler unit
    • Tubing and Monitoring console etc
  • Limitation/Problems :
    • Requires full anticoagulation
    • Can cause micro embolism
    • Initiates Systemic Inflammatory Response

Complications of CPB

Slide 86
  • 1. Systemic inflammatory response due to contact of blood with the non-endothelialized surface of CPB circuit resulting in increased capillary permeability, interstitial edema, and subsequent organ dysfunction.
  • 2. Coagulopathy caused by platelet dysfunction as well as dilution and consumption of coagulation factors.
  • 3. Hemolysis.
  • 4. Cerebrovascular accident

Cardiac compression (Tamponade)

Slide 89
  • Effects of cardiac compression (Tamponade):
  • Cardiac compression prevents proper relaxation and diastolic filling of the heart. This results in:
  • Systemic venous congestion.
  • Low cardiac output.

Clinical features of Tamponade

Slide 90
  • Signs of low cardiac output: small pulse volume, low B.P., tachycardia.
  • Signs of systemic venous congestion: congested neck veins, kussmaul sign (increase in jugular venous pressure with inspiration) is unusual.
  • Signs of pericardial effusion
  • Pulsus Paradoxus.
  • Shock in severe cases.

Slide 104

  • Is the patient fit to undergo the planned operation
